chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, said:
The one in Ihram pays the ransom of the prey from wherever he attains it.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The one in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.فِدَاءَ: Ransom/compensation for a specific act or item
key_terms.مِنْ حَيْثُ: From wherever / from the place where

ai.seo_question: Where should a person in Ihram obtain the ransom for the game they killed?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan, clarifies the practical application of fidyah by anchoring the valuation to the local market conditions where the prey was killed, ensuring fairness in compensation. In Shia jurisprudence, this principle prevents arbitrary assessment by tying the penalty to the immediate economic context of the incident. It reflects the juristic emphasis on contextual equity when enforcing ritual prohibitions during Hajj or Umrah.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, and Safwan, from Muawiya Bin Ammar,
‘Heasws said: ‘The one in Ihraam would pay the ransom of the hunted prey from wherever he attains it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr and Safwan from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who hunts in the state of Ihram must pay the ransom where he has hunted.’”
